A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAK-UCB/RFF-UCB research. Their main texts, figures, equations and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite the expanded LLM scope and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original online-selection experiments with pretrained text-to-image models and synthetic image-generation, captioning and video setups, including results averaged over 20 trials.

after.justification: V3 retains original generative-model experiments and adds empirical LLM selection results for code generation and Sudoku solving.

M1.justification: The per-arm kernel-regression/UCB design remains. V3 replaces random-phase cosine RFF features with paired sine/cosine features, changes practical selection scores to mean plus eta times uncertainty, and confines approximation bonuses to the theoretical Sup variant. These are bounded refinements of the existing procedures.

E1.justification: V3 adds LLM code completion using HumanEval in Figure 1 and BigCodeBench in Setup 2, HumanEval-X code translation, and random 9-by-9 Sudoku problems. The earlier MS-COCO and MSR-VTT coverage, synthetic expert setups and adaptation scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Random selection is added to retained comparisons, while LinUCB, PAK-UCB-lin and Naive-KRR remain in appendix plots. Figures 30–31 additionally compare RFF-UCB-RBF against full-kernel PAK-UCB-RBF on accuracy; v2 compared that pair only on running time.

E3.justification: V3 reports revised exploration settings, replacing eta=1 with sqrt(2 log(2G/delta)), delta=0.05, and changes the RFF default from 50 features to D=200. OPR changes from a prompt-type reference to a per-prompt best model estimated from five responses. New LLM protocols introduce binary correctness rewards, a 164-task BigCodeBench subset and Sudoku problems with 5–30 blanks. These reported revisions do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing adaptation tests, synthetic noise setups and four hyperparameter studies are retained. V3 adds controlled full-RBF versus RFF accuracy comparisons on Sudoku and code generation in Figures 30–31, directly examining approximation quality beyond the earlier timing comparison. Adaptation-result curves are also revised.

E5.justification: Twenty-trial averaging and graphical uncertainty reporting are retained. V3 newly specifies five responses per prompt/model for estimating the reference-best model used in OPR. This adds statistical estimation and repeated-sampling information without establishing an increase in the existing trial counts.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial LLM results, including hard-Sudoku success rates of 70.82% for o3-mini versus 50.42% for Deepseek-Chat. Retained curves also change: RFF's final OPR in the Stable Diffusion/PixArt comparison is approximately 0.55 in v2 Figure 2 and 0.61 in v3 Figure 8, under revised settings. Code-result attribution remains ambiguous because Section 6.2 names Qwen-Plus while Figures 5 and 20 name Claude-3.5-Haiku.

T1.justification: Appendices A–B substantially revise the staged-regret and RFF approximation proofs while retaining the square-root regret order. V3 introduces alpha<=1, revised feature/error schedules and a time-dependent variance-error bound replacing the earlier c-dependent bound, and corrects the KRR penalty to a squared norm. However, Equation (22) introduces an inverse-matrix norm bound of 1/(1+alpha) that is not guaranteed by the stated kernel assumptions.

C1.justification: LLM selection moves from future work in v2's conclusion to an explicit demonstrated application in v3's title, introduction and conclusion. V3 also qualifies the introduction's regret claim as applying to a variant, whereas v2 directly attributed it to PAK-UCB. The central prompt-dependent selection contribution remains.

C2.justification: V3 adds a lower-variance rationale for the paired RFF representation and interprets the matched-kernel experiments as preserving predictive performance while reducing computation. It also discusses adaptability relative to offline routers and adds cost-aware selection as a future direction. Earlier interpretations concerning prompt-dependent rankings and diversity extensions remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds code-access information, identifies the specific CLIP encoder, documents 768-dimensional RoBERTa/CodeBERT inputs, and supplies LLM prompt examples and additional settings. V2's feature-caching disclosure disappears. Reproducibility remains imperfect: v3 calls D=200 '200-dimensional' despite defining a 2D-dimensional map, and uses gamma when specifying its sigma-parameterized RBF kernel.

R1.justification: V3 adds substantive positioning against offline prompt-to-model methods, including Stylus, DiffusionGPT and Prompt-to-Leaderboard, and against unconditional-model bandit selection using FID-UCB and Mixture-UCB. It also acknowledges existing arm-specific linear bandits and expands LLM and RFF references, while removing several older generation citations.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the introduction, kernel/RFF explanations and experimental narrative. It reverses the preliminary-subsection order, moves RFF pseudocode into the appendix, and reorganizes the former four appendices into three with redistributed proofs and experimental subsections. Terminology also changes from O2B to OtB and RFF-UCB to RFF-UCB-RBF.

P2.justification: V3 adds workflow diagrams, LLM examples and prompt illustrations, and approximation-accuracy plots. It redesigns Figure 1, rearranges and simplifies main comparison panels, and displays OtB instead of OPR in the main T2I summary while retaining both metrics in the appendix. Earlier image examples, adaptation plots and ablation displays are matched across their relocations.

improvement.justification: V3 turns v2's proposed LLM extension into experiments and adds matched-kernel accuracy checks, strengthening empirical support; code and encoder documentation also improve inspectability. However, conflicting Qwen-Plus/Claude-3.5-Haiku attribution obscures the new code results, RFF settings remain inconsistent, and the revised proof introduces the unsupported inverse-norm bound in Equation (22). These problems affect both new evidence and theoretical justification, preventing a reliable judgment of the net quality change.
